author: @FrankCurzio
text:
Scared money is stampeding into bonds.

Treasuries are headed for their longest winning streak in almost five months as AI doubts sink stocks worldwide.

Global stocks are on track for their longest losing streak in over three years. South Korea and Taiwan both dropped at least 4%. Japan's Nikkei fell 4.5%.

Yet the 10-year yield was still 5.06% on Nov 19. That's ABOVE the 5% line I called the tripwire last week.

And 30-year mortgages sat at 7.11%. Nobody is borrowing cheaper yet.

Some Fed officials still want another hike. So short rates stay pinned while panic piles into long bonds... a market bracing for more pain.

Memory chip prices keep climbing, yet chip suppliers get dumped with everything else.

Taiwan's market drops 4% while the company getting every AI order first is still accelerating. That's fear talking.

Taiwan Semi ($TSM) is a buy for me on this selloff.

-

For anyone new here, I'm Frank. 30 years on Wall Street, and I post what's moving the market as it happens. Follow me @FrankCurzio for more.
